input.question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?
input.ground_truth: I'm not sure if you're going to get a proper ELI5 answer to this: understanding why things run that fast requires understanding how computers are designed and the network architecture of the Internet - not exactly light reading. But to give more details about investors: yes, investment firms will pay out the nose for real estate as close to the stock exchange as possible, so that their trading servers will have as little lag as they can. Every last millisecond counts.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How are online games like CoD or WoW able to coordinate information from so many different players so fast?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and all your friends want to play a big game together in the same playground at the same time. You all have your own toys (that’s like your computers or phones), and you all want to see each other’s toys and what everyone is doing, right?

Now, imagine there is a super helpful teacher (that’s like the game’s server) in the middle of the playground. Every time you do something—like jump or run—the teacher quickly tells all your friends what you did. The teacher is really, really fast and good at talking to everyone at once.

So, when you shoot in a game like CoD or cast a spell in WoW, your toy (your device) tells the teacher what you did. The teacher then quickly tells all the other toys what happened. That’s how everyone sees what everyone else is doing, all at the same time, without getting confused!

That’s how online games can have lots of people playing together and everything stays in sync so quickly! 🎮✨
